analysis:
Examined the ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift patch plus base/head text, and the one-line ProviderLoop+EngineV2.swift patch (resliceGateGeneration &+= 1 after isReslicing = true). Only the patch hunk for EngineV2.swift was supplied, with no surrounding source.

Changed behavior in capacityRefreshTick: new calls to superviseTransitions(), sweepAutopilotCachedBuilds(), refreshAutopilotDownloadStorage() and refreshAutopilotInventoryRegistration(). These are local actor-isolated housekeeping and Autopilot inventory hooks. Their implementations were not supplied, so their effects are unverified. In particular, refreshAutopilotInventoryRegistration may send inventory to the coordinator (TB-002) and sweepAutopilotCachedBuilds may delete files on disk (TB-003/A-004). I saw nothing that opens an auth, encryption, attestation or plaintext path, but the reviewer of those functions should check that inventory data sent to the coordinator is not sensitive and that any deletion is confined to the owner-controlled cache path.

In updateAggregateCapacity, reclaimableMlx now subtracts min(mlxUsed, autopilotHeldWeightBytes()). The saturating min prevents underflow. The change only makes advertised free_for_load_gb more conservative, so it cannot cause over-advertising of capacity. The held-bytes helper was not seen.

The reslice generation counter uses a wrapping increment (&+=), so it cannot trap. How it is consumed (probably to detect a stale gate) was not supplied.

No prompt, key, or attestation handling changed. T-041 (prefix cache) lists ProviderLoop+EngineV2.swift as an affected file, but this change touches only a gate generation counter and does not alter cache TTL, naming or crypto. No finding. Residual uncertainty: the unseen helper implementations.
